newsitem.title: USA: U.S. sweetener industry to challenge Mexico ruling.
newsitem.headline: U.S. sweetener industry to challenge Mexico ruling.

text.p: U.S. corn processors plan to ask U.S. Trade Representative Charlene Barshefsky to challenge Mexico's recent decision to slap duties as high as $175 per tonne on U.S. high-fructose exports, the head of the U.S. Corn Refiners Association said Monday.

"We do not believe that Mexico's domestic sugar industry has the legal standing to bring a dumping claim against a non- like product such as high-fructose sweeteners," Chuck Conner, head of the group, told a meeting of the U.S. Feed Grains Council. "We will take this issue to the World Trade Organization, if necessary."

Mexico issued a preliminary ruling about two weeks ago to impose duties on high-fructose imports at the request of Mexican sugar producers, Conner said. The Mexican government will review public comments on the ruling until early October, then issue a final decision.

"But in the meantime, duties are being applied to any U.S. exports, in some cases as much as $175 per tonne," he said. The U.S. sweetener industry has struggled with depressed prices for some time, and the new duty makes U.S. products uncompetitive, Conner said.
High fructose sweeteners are produced from corn for use in flavoring beverages and foods, and account for about 515 million bushels of corn annually.
